title: The Lookout Tower
hook: The ranger gave me one rule for the fire lookout tower: after dark, the trapdoor stays shut... no matter who's knocking.
lines: I spent last summer alone in a fire lookout tower, sixty feet up. The only way in is a trapdoor in the floor.
The ranger who drove me up tapped the latch and said, After dark, this stays shut. No matter who's knocking.
I laughed. The nearest road was eleven miles away.
On my third night, I saw a flashlight down in the pines... moving slowly toward the tower.
Then the stairs started creaking. One step at a time... all the way up.
Something knocked on the trapdoor. Three times.
Then the ranger's voice said my name. Storm's rolling in, kid. Let me up.
My hand was on the latch... when I looked out the window.
No clouds. Just stars, all the way to the mountains. And no headlights on the road.
So I sat on that trapdoor until the knocking stopped... and the stairs went quiet.
I was still shaking when I heard it again.
A soft tap... on the glass behind me. Sixty feet up.
And the ranger's voice whispered, That's fine. I'll wait up here.
